title: Rank customers by spend
context: The Growth team wants a leaderboard of top spenders for the loyalty launch.
task: Return first_name, last_name, total_spend (delivered orders, 2 decimals) and rank_position using RANK() ordered by spend descending.
hint: Aggregate first, then RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(...) DESC).
answer: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, ROUND(SUM(o.total_amount), 2) AS total_spend, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(o.total_amount) DESC) AS rank_position FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'delivered' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

title: Most recent order per customer
context: Support needs the latest order on every customer profile.
task: Return customer_id, order_id and order_date for each customer's most recent order (ties broken by highest order_id).
hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, order_id DESC) = 1.
answer: SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date FROM (SELECT customer_id, order_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC, order_id DESC) AS rn FROM orders) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Top 2 products per category by price
context: Each category page features its two priciest items.
task: Return category, name and price for the top 2 priced products in each category (DENSE_RANK, so ties are included).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) <= 2.
answer: SELECT category, name, price FROM (SELECT category, name, price, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS rk FROM products) WHERE rk <= 2;

title: Cumulative delivered revenue by month
context: The finance chart shows year-to-date revenue growing month by month.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), revenue and cumulative_revenue (running sum ordered by month), both rounded to 2 decimals, for delivered orders.
hint: SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) on top of a monthly CTE.
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_revenue FROM m;

title: Month-over-month revenue change
context: Leadership asks how each month compared with the previous one.
task: Return month, revenue and mom_change = revenue minus previous month's revenue (NULL for the first month), delivered orders only, 2 decimals, ordered by month.
hint: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month).
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, SUM(total_amount) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' GROUP BY month) SELECT month, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, ROUND(revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS mom_change FROM m;

title: Days between consecutive orders
context: Retention analysis looks at purchase gaps.
task: For every order that has a previous order by the same customer, return customer_id, order_id and gap_days = days since that customer's previous order (integer).
hint: LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, order_id), then julianday difference; exclude NULL gaps.
answer: SELECT customer_id, order_id, gap_days FROM (SELECT customer_id, order_id, CAST(julianday(order_date) - julianday(LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, order_id)) AS INTEGER) AS gap_days FROM orders) WHERE gap_days IS NOT NULL;

title: Customer spend quartiles
context: Segmentation splits customers into four spend bands.
task: Return customer_id, total_spend (all orders, 2 decimals) and quartile = NTILE(4) ordered by total_spend descending (1 = highest spenders).
hint: Aggregate in a CTE, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC).
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spend FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT customer_id, ROUND(total_spend, 2) AS total_spend, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY total_spend DESC) AS quartile FROM s;

title: Product share within category
context: Category managers need each SKU's share of category revenue.
task: Return category, name and pct_of_category = product revenue / category revenue * 100 (1 decimal), using all order items.
hint: SUM(rev) OVER (PARTITION BY category).
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT p.category, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS rev FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id) SELECT category, name, ROUND(rev * 100.0 / SUM(rev) OVER (PARTITION BY category), 1) AS pct_of_category FROM r;

title: 3-month moving average of orders
context: Smooth out seasonality on the order-volume chart.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM), order_count and ma3 = average order_count over the current and two preceding months (2 decimals), ordered by month.
hint: AVG(...) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
answer: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY month) SELECT month, order_count, ROUND(AVG(order_count) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS ma3 FROM m;

title: First product each customer ever bought
context: Growth studies which products drive first purchases.
task: Return customer_id and first_product = name of the product on the earliest order line (earliest order_date, then lowest item_id), one row per customer who ordered.
hint: FIRST_VALUE(p.name) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, item_id), then DISTINCT.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id, FIRST_VALUE(p.name) OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date, oi.item_id) AS first_product FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

title: Repeat-purchase rate by signup year
context: Does a customer's signup cohort predict repeat buying?
task: Return signup_year and repeat_rate_pct = customers with 2+ orders / customers with 1+ orders * 100 (1 decimal), grouped by signup year.
hint: CTE of per-customer order counts joined to customers; conditional SUM over COUNT.
answer: WITH oc AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', c.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS signup_year, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN oc.n >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 1) AS repeat_rate_pct FROM customers c JOIN oc ON oc.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY signup_year;

title: Customers active in consecutive months
context: Month-to-month retention is the core health metric.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and retained = number of customers who ordered in that month AND in the previous calendar month, ordered by month. Only include months with retained > 0.
hint: Distinct (customer, month) pairs; self-join where the other month = date(month || '-01', '-1 month').
answer: WITH cm AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month FROM orders) SELECT a.month, COUNT(*) AS retained FROM cm a JOIN cm b ON b.customer_id = a.customer_id AND b.month = strftime('%Y-%m', date(a.month || '-01', '-1 month')) GROUP BY a.month ORDER BY a.month;

title: RFM snapshot
context: The CRM team scores customers on recency, frequency and monetary value.
task: For each customer with orders, return customer_id, recency_days = days from their last order_date to '2025-07-31' (integer), frequency = order count, monetary = total spend (2 decimals).
hint: julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(order_date)).
answer: SELECT customer_id, CAST(julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(order_date)) AS INTEGER) AS recency_days, COUNT(*) AS frequency, ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS monetary FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

title: Products making up the top 80% of revenue
context: Classic ABC analysis: which SKUs drive most revenue?
task: Return name and revenue (2 decimals) for products whose cumulative revenue share (ordered by revenue desc, ties by name) is at or below 80% of total, plus the first product that crosses 80%.
hint: Running SUM OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, name) compared to 0.8 * total; include the row whose previous cumulative was below 80%.
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS rev FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id), c AS (SELECT name, rev, SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, name ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_cum, SUM(rev) OVER () AS total FROM r) SELECT name, ROUND(rev, 2) AS revenue FROM c WHERE COALESCE(prev_cum, 0) < 0.8 * total;

title: Longest streak of consecutive order days
context: Ops wants to know the longest run of days with at least one order.
task: Return streak_start, streak_end and streak_days for the single longest streak of consecutive calendar days with orders (ties broken by earliest start).
hint: Distinct dates, ROW_NUMBER, then group by date(d, -rn days).
answer: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT order_date FROM orders), g AS (SELECT order_date, date(order_date, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY order_date) || ' days') AS grp FROM d) SELECT MIN(order_date) AS streak_start, MAX(order_date) AS streak_end, COUNT(*) AS streak_days FROM g GROUP BY grp ORDER BY streak_days DESC, streak_start LIMIT 1;

title: Generate every month in 2024
context: The chart must show months with zero orders too.
task: Using a recursive CTE, return month (YYYY-MM) and order_count for every month of 2024, including months with 0 orders, ordered by month.
hint: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS (SELECT '2024-01-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(m, '+1 month') ...) then LEFT JOIN.
answer: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS (SELECT '2024-01-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(m, '+1 month') FROM months WHERE m < '2024-12-01') SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', m) AS month, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM months LEFT JOIN orders o ON strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) = strftime('%Y-%m', m) GROUP BY m ORDER BY m;

title: Number series 1 to 10
context: Warm-up: generate rows without a table.
task: Return a single column n with the integers 1 through 10 using a recursive CTE, in ascending order.
hint: WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 10).
answer: WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM seq WHERE n < 10) SELECT n FROM seq;

title: Median order value
context: AOV is skewed by big orders; leadership wants the median.
task: Return median_order = the median total_amount across all orders (average of the two middle values if even count), 2 decimals.
hint: ROW_NUMBER and COUNT(*) OVER (); keep rows where rn is in ((cnt+1)/2, (cnt+2)/2).
answer: WITH o AS (SELECT total_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_amount) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt FROM orders) SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_amount), 2) AS median_order FROM o WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);

title: Products in the top 10% by price
context: The 'luxury' badge goes on the priciest decile.
task: Return name and price for products whose price is in the top 10% (PERCENT_RANK ordered by price ascending >= 0.9).
hint: PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY price).
answer: SELECT name, price FROM (SELECT name, price, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY price) AS pr FROM products) WHERE pr >= 0.9;

title: Customers whose every order was delivered
context: The 'flawless' badge requires zero cancellations or returns.
task: Return customer_id for customers with at least one order where all of their orders have status 'delivered'.
hint: GROUP BY customer, HAVING COUNT(*) = SUM(status = 'delivered').
answer: SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) = SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END);

title: Customers who bought from every category
context: Cross-category buyers are the most valuable segment.
task: Return customer_id for customers who have ordered at least one product from every category in products.
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT category) per customer = total categories.
answer: SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category) FROM products);

title: Products frequently bought together
context: 'Frequently bought together' needs product pairs from the same order.
task: Return product_a, product_b (names, with product_a's id < product_b's id) and times_together = number of distinct orders containing both, for pairs that co-occur in 2 or more orders.
hint: Self-join order_items on order_id with product_id inequality; count distinct order_id.
answer: SELECT pa.name AS product_a, pb.name AS product_b, COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS times_together FROM order_items a JOIN order_items b ON a.order_id = b.order_id AND a.product_id < b.product_id JOIN products pa ON pa.product_id = a.product_id JOIN products pb ON pb.product_id = b.product_id GROUP BY a.product_id, b.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) >= 2;

title: Reviews before purchase
context: Trust & Safety flags reviews written by people who never bought the item.
task: Return review_id, customer_id and product_id for reviews where the customer has no order containing that product.
hint: NOT EXISTS across orders + order_items.
answer: SELECT r.review_id, r.customer_id, r.product_id FROM reviews r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = r.customer_id AND oi.product_id = r.product_id);

title: Salary vs department average
context: HR flags employees far from their department's mean.
task: Return first_name, department, salary and diff_from_avg = salary minus the department's average salary (2 decimals), for employees more than 5000 above or below it.
hint: AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department).
answer: SELECT first_name, department, salary, ROUND(diff, 2) AS diff_from_avg FROM (SELECT first_name, department, salary, salary - AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS diff FROM employees) WHERE ABS(diff) > 5000;

title: Second-highest salary per department
context: Succession planning looks at the number-two earner.
task: Return department and second_salary = the second-highest distinct salary in each department (departments with only one salary are excluded).
hint: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) = 2.
answer: SELECT department, salary AS second_salary FROM (SELECT department, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rk FROM employees) WHERE rk = 2;

title: Category units by year
context: A wide report with one column per year.
task: Return category, units_2024 and units_2025 = total quantity ordered in each year (0 if none).
hint: SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024' THEN quantity ELSE 0 END).
answer: SELECT p.category, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.order_date) = '2024' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2024, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.order_date) = '2025' THEN oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2025 FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

title: Review rate per product
context: Which products get reviewed relative to how often they sell?
task: Return name, orders_count = distinct orders containing the product, reviews_count, and reviews_per_order (2 decimals), for products with at least one order. Use separate CTEs to avoid join fan-out.
hint: Aggregate orders and reviews in separate CTEs, then LEFT JOIN reviews onto orders.
answer: WITH oc AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_count FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id), rc AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS reviews_count FROM reviews GROUP BY product_id) SELECT p.name, oc.orders_count, COALESCE(rc.reviews_count, 0) AS reviews_count, ROUND(COALESCE(rc.reviews_count, 0) * 1.0 / oc.orders_count, 2) AS reviews_per_order FROM oc JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oc.product_id LEFT JOIN rc ON rc.product_id = oc.product_id;

title: Cumulative unique customers by month
context: Growth tracks how the customer base compounds over time.
task: Return month (YYYY-MM) and cumulative_customers = number of distinct customers whose first order was in or before that month, for every month with orders, ordered by month.
hint: First-order month per customer, count per month, then running SUM.
answer: WITH f AS (SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(order_date)) AS first_month FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id), m AS (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month FROM orders) SELECT m.month, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM f WHERE f.first_month <= m.month) AS cumulative_customers FROM m ORDER BY m.month;

title: Weeks of stock remaining
context: Supply chain estimates how long inventory lasts at the current sales rate.
task: Return name, stock, weekly_rate = total units sold / 78 (about 18 months, 2 decimals) and weeks_left = stock / weekly_rate (1 decimal), for products with sales, ordered by weeks_left ascending.
hint: Guard the divide with * 1.0; ORDER BY the computed column.
answer: WITH s AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity) * 1.0 / 78 AS weekly_rate FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id) SELECT p.name, p.stock, ROUND(s.weekly_rate, 2) AS weekly_rate, ROUND(p.stock / s.weekly_rate, 1) AS weeks_left FROM products p JOIN s ON s.product_id = p.product_id ORDER BY weeks_left, p.name;

title: Best-selling product per country
context: Country managers want their local number-one SKU.
task: Return country, name and units for the top-selling product (by quantity) in each customer country; break ties by name ascending.
hint: Aggregate by country+product, then ROW_NUMBER() PARTITION BY country.
answer: WITH t AS (SELECT c.country, p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY c.country, p.product_id) SELECT country, name, units FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY units DESC, name) AS rn FROM t) WHERE rn = 1;

title: Customers with no order in the last 180 days
context: As of 2025-07-31, who has gone quiet?
task: Return customer_id and last_order = MAX(order_date) for customers whose most recent order is more than 180 days before '2025-07-31'.
hint: HAVING julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(order_date)) > 180.
answer: SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING julianday('2025-07-31') - julianday(MAX(order_date)) > 180;

title: Products whose ratings are falling
context: Quality flags items whose recent reviews are worse than their early ones.
task: Return name, early_avg and late_avg (2 decimals) where early_avg is the average of the product's first 2 reviews by date and late_avg the average of its last 2, for products with at least 4 reviews and late_avg < early_avg.
hint: ROW_NUMBER ascending and descending per product, then conditional AVG.
answer: WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, rating, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY review_date, review_id) AS rn_a, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY review_date DESC, review_id DESC) AS rn_d, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id) AS n FROM reviews) SELECT p.name, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn_a <= 2 THEN rating END), 2) AS early_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN rn_d <= 2 THEN rating END), 2) AS late_avg FROM r JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id WHERE n >= 4 GROUP BY r.product_id HAVING late_avg < early_avg;

title: Fan-out trap: revenue and reviews in one query
context: A junior analyst joined orders, items and reviews in one go and got inflated revenue. Fix it.
task: Return category, revenue = SUM(quantity * unit_price) over all order items (2 decimals) and review_count = number of reviews for products in that category, with no double counting.
hint: Aggregate revenue and reviews separately (CTEs) before joining on category.
answer: WITH rev AS (SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category), rv AS (SELECT p.category, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM reviews r JOIN products p ON p.product_id = r.product_id GROUP BY p.category) SELECT rev.category, ROUND(rev.revenue, 2) AS revenue, COALESCE(rv.review_count, 0) AS review_count FROM rev LEFT JOIN rv ON rv.category = rev.category;
